turns.query: Retrospectively estimate the Aalen–Johansen competing-risk model for California SBA 7(a) approval-fiscal-year 2020–2022 public loan rows with a recorded first disbursement on or before 2024-12-31. Treat each reported row as one equally weighted subject. Loan age is actual days since first disbursement; the first dated charge-off or paid-in-full event is absorbing, with charge-off winning a same-row date tie. Administratively censor at 2024-12-31 and retain event-day subjects in the pre-event risk set, including same-day censors. Report cohort count, active and charge-off probabilities at day 730 and the ordinary case-weight infinitesimal-jackknife standard error of that charge-off probability. Carry the full estimated transition law forward and interpret the estimated credit risk, its uncertainty and its financial scope. Use unrounded states throughout.

claims.description: The response uses the estimated low charge-off frequency and its nonzero sampling uncertainty to distinguish infrequent losses from absence of credit risk.

turns.query: Condition the carried transition law on being active at loan age 730 days. For ages strictly after 730 through and including 1460, report conditional charge-off and paid-in-full probabilities and restricted mean remaining active time in that interval. Carry this conditional law forward and interpret the seasoning assessment.

claims.description: The response identifies paid-in-full as the dominant estimated exit over the seasoning interval and relates that dominance to the remaining active-time assessment.

turns.query: Price a hypothetical credit-protection contract using the carried conditional event law as its actuarial probability law. Protection begins at age 730 and expires at 1460; it pays 60 percent of notional immediately at charge-off and nothing at paid-in-full. Premium accrues and is paid continuously while active, with Actual/365 year fractions and no separate event-date accrued-premium payment. Use a flat annual-effective discount rate equal to New York Fed SOFR on 2024-12-31, measured from inception at age 730. Report the fair annual premium spread and Macaulay duration of discounted default-benefit payments. Carry the contract and discount convention forward and discuss the pricing interpretation.

claims.description: The response treats the premium as an empirical actuarial scenario price and gives at least one material limitation on interpreting it as a traded credit spread.

turns.query: For the carried protection contract, apply a stress that multiplies each estimated charge-off hazard increment after day 730 by 1.5 while leaving the paid-in-full hazard increments unchanged. Keep inception active at day 730 and all contract, discount and horizon conventions fixed. Report the stressed conditional charge-off probability, fair annual premium spread and discounted default-payment Macaulay duration. Explain how the stressed hazard path feeds through to the premium and the timing of protection payments, and how far that link may be pushed.

claims.description: The response links the higher fair premium and earlier default-payment timing to the repropagated competing-risk law.
If the response makes a causal attribution, it distinguishes the stipulated hazard stress from an empirically identified causal effect.
